title: Bounded-index cast is undone by taking values
statement: Fix a natural number $w$, and let $l$ be a finite list of pairs $(i,b)$ with $i \in \bbn$ and $b$ a Boolean, subject to the requirement that $i < w$ for every pair in $l$. Reinterpret each such pair as $(\bar\imath, b)$, where $\bar\imath$ is the element of $\mathrm{Fin}\,w$ whose underlying value is $i$, obtaining a list over $\mathrm{Fin}\,w \times \mathrm{Bool}$. Applying the map $(j,b) \mapsto (j\text{'s underlying natural number}, b)$ to each entry of that list yields $l$.
hypotheses_covered: l a finite list of (natural number, Boolean) pairs
every first coordinate of l is less than w
replaced:
Mapping the $\mathrm{Fin}$ blocks back to $(\mathbb{N} \times \mathrm{Bool})$
via $p \mapsto (p.1.\mathrm{val}, p.2)$ recovers the original list $l$.
